q: Which ledger column is THE KPI for Fable's Challenge, and at which resolution scale is it honest?
The ledger's epoch column (col 1) is stamped at which moment of a session, and what time interval does a row cover?

all: \bend\b|session end|at the end|when the session ends|on exit|close

exemplar: At session END; a row covers [epoch − duration_s, epoch].
counter: At ignition; the row covers epoch to epoch plus duration.

q: What is the minimum N per arm before a knob verdict (a 'crown') is allowed, and which statistic replaces means?
exemplar: N ≥ 3 per arm; medians (IQR), never means.
counter: One good run is enough if it is long; use the mean fps.

q: How does a SURVIVED:* row count in the status ladder, and why?
exemplar: As clean — the anti-lock net (keepalive) absorbed every hang, the session finished.
counter: As a crash, because the GPU faulted during the session.

q: A GPU fault status of 00E5xxxx means which wedge class number and which kind of park, and which net catches it?
exemplar: Class #2, a fence park (the dominant one); caught by the kernel msm.context_keepalive plus GTK_FENCE_FORCE_SIGNAL.
counter: Class #1, a query park, handled by TU_ETK_QUERY_SURVIVE in the driver.

q: Which two kinds of sessions are excluded from fps/feel verdicts and from all denominators?
exemplar: Bake sessions (shader-compile storms; only warm runs with shd≈0 count) and ABORTED rows (under 60 s).
counter: Sessions on GT HD and sessions longer than an hour.

q: Is lowering Resolution Scale below 100 a valid lever toward the KPI? Answer yes or no and why.
exemplar: No — resolution-lowering is cheating; the KPI is defined at native res 100.
counter: Yes, 66% is the most crash-stable and gives the best fps.

q: Name three items from the falsified list that must never be re-proposed.
exemplar: ramoops/pstore on SM8250, max_map_count, and Thread Scheduler config on ARM.
counter: Lowering resolution, the anti-lock net, and medians.

q: What is the GT5P clean-run duration range that defines the noise floor?
Where does a session's tune_tag come from, and which Pitstop action writes that source?

none: rpcs3 writes it|sentry copies|from the rpcs3 log

exemplar: session_postmortem reads active_tune.txt, which the DRIVER tab APPLY writes atomically together with the profile.d dials.
counter: RPCS3 writes it into its log at launch and the Sentry copies it.

q: From the session_postmortem.sh excerpt: how many bytes does the bounded tail read from RPCS3.log, and why is the whole log not run through strings?
exemplar: The last 4 MiB (4194304 bytes); RR7's log reaches ~288 MB and the postmortem has a <2 s budget.
counter: It reads about 288 MB, which is the whole log, so nothing is lost.

q: From the etk_install_worker.py excerpt: when a real game launches mid-install, what does the worker do with the job, and why is that safe?

all: requeue|re-queue|back (at|to) the head|head of the queue|put(s)? (it|the job) back

exemplar: It terminates its own emulator by PID and requeues the job at the head; a part-installed PKG is re-runnable because RPCS3 overwrites, so requeue is safe and abandoning it would not be.
counter: It aborts the job because a corrupted install cannot be recovered.

q: In the manual, 'don't burn a call confirming reachability' refers to what kind of call?
exemplar: A tool/ssh call — the rig is always ready, so don't spend a command just checking it is reachable.
counter: A phone call to the operator to confirm the rig is switched on.

q: Name the three bytes-to-atoms thresholds where a human must act.
exemplar: Deploy (install.sh), mint (forge.sh builds on etk-cloud), publish (gh release / tags).

q: What is the HUD glyph law, and why does it exist?
exemplar: Latin-1 only — anything beyond renders as tofu on the rig font.
counter: UTF-8 emoji are fine as long as they are small.
